pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' and a CHECK constraint. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js `item` renders '— high' or '— low' and nothing for normal. The 'AC-2' test asserts the exact list items.
The 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal. The query is filtered and ordered by id.
The 'AC-4' test checks the unfiltered list in id order.
The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.
The 'AC-6' test checks a 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__. The Set check in src/index.js enforces it.

The behaviour is implemented, and an unnamed test and the 'No match' and 'Empty table' state tests exercise it. But commit 6170016 ('Follow-up edits') renamed the test to drop 'AC-7', so no test names AC-7. The spec requires each item to be named by a test. I could not run the suite (vitest is not installed here).
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. The 'AC-8' test asserts it. The traffic-config check accepts a query string.

findings.what: The last commit, a bot-authored 'Follow-up edits', removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test title. No test now names AC-7, so the item is unmet by the rule that each item is named by its proving test. The PR body still says the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7:' in the test title. Revert 6170016, or at least explain why it was needed.

findings.what: The PR claims test/priority.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8. This is false for AC-7 after the final commit. The PR also doesn't mention the late 'Follow-up edits' commit.
findings.fix: Fix the test name so the claim is true, and describe all commits.

findings.what: The route regex now accepts any query string. The error message still says 'paths starting with "/"'. The README doesn't mention that routes may carry a query.
findings.fix: Update the message and the traffic docs to mention optional query strings.

lenses.note: The spec is present. Behaviour matches it; nothing extra was added beyond the traffic-check relaxation, which AC-8 needs.
AC-7 is unnamed by any test after the last commit. The other items are met, and the four state rows have tests.
The tests assert behaviour. A test title was edited in the last commit to drop its AC id. I could not run npm test because vitest is not installed in this copy.
The README documents the filter. The traffic docs don't say routes may now carry a query string.
The input is validated against an allowlist and the query is parameterised. No defects found.
Titles are HTML-escaped, the priority value is allowlisted and the SQL is bound. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches no UI style or layout files. It only changes the markup that src/index.js renders.
No browser or UI flow was available. The list page is covered by HTML-assertion tests only.
The claim that tests cover AC-1 to AC-8 is false for AC-7, and the final commit isn't mentioned. The title is under 72 characters.
